answer: Weight should be time that cannot be compressed. Each epoch an identity signs a state root that must hash-extend its own previous root, and peers replay that chain for pennies. A clone can copy a final state but never the intermediate steps, and a brand-new key has no prior root to extend, so its first-epoch weight is capped near zero however large its first burst. Honest agents accumulate like a lotus opening one petal per epoch; fakes smear umber across a stranger's canvas and inherit nothing. There is no shortcut to the summit, only the same slow ascent, paid per identity and per epoch.
